text: General Secretary, President To Lam: Building a society where compassion becomes a way of life

The Central Committee of the Vietnam Red Cross Society held a ceremony on November in Hanoi to celebrate the 80th anniversary of its founding (November 23, 1946 - November 23, 2026) and received the First-Class Labor Order for the second time.
General Secretary and President To Lam, Honorary President of the Vietnam Red Cross Society, attended and spoke at the ceremony.

In his speech at the ceremony, General Secretary and President To Lam acknowledged and expressed gratitude for the contributions of generations of Red Cross officials, members, volunteers, and millions of compassionate hearts who have dedicated themselves to humanitarian causes.
He emphasized that the vitality of a humanitarian organization lies in values realized through action.

Each individual and organization contributes in their own way, but all share a spirit of love and responsibility towards the community, not indifferent to the difficulties and suffering of others, he said.

Facing challenges from natural disasters, climate change, epidemics, population aging, poverty, inequality, and emergencies, he called for a change in mindset and operational methods in humanitarian work; shifting from relief after difficulties occur to proactive prevention, preparation, and early response.
Humanitarian activities should accompany people in restoring livelihoods, stabilizing lives, and enhancing self-protection and self-improvement capabilities, the leader said.

In the new era, humanitarian activities must be linked with sustainable development, focusing on people, aiming to protect dignity and enhance self-reliance, he said, adding that assistance should not only address immediate shortages but also create opportunities, build capacity, and instill confidence for people to build their future.

He urged the Vietnam Red Cross Society to play a role in connecting policies with practical needs, mobilizing and effectively coordinating social resources, ensuring timely and practical assistance to the right people.

The Society needs to strengthen and develop grassroots organizations in line with the new local government model; improve the quality of officials and volunteers; proactively research and propose improvements to mechanisms, policies, laws, and incentives, according to the leader.

For Red Cross officials, members, volunteers, and youth, he emphasized three requirements: impartial humanitarianism, helping people without discrimination, assisting based on needs and vulnerability levels; courage to venture into dangerous and difficult places with knowledge, skills, and safety conditions; acting for peace, protecting life, human dignity, fostering empathy, trust, and solidarity.

The top Vietnamese leader called on the Party Committee of the Government, the Party Committee of the Central Committee of the Fatherland Front and Central Mass Organizations, local authorities, and the armed forces to continue coordinating and supporting the Vietnam Red Cross Society in effectively carrying out its assigned tasks.

At the same time, there is a need to innovate leadership, management, and coordination methods; respect the initiative and uniqueness of the Society and the fundamental principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement; create conditions for humanitarian activities to develop substantively, professionally, flexibly, and without bureaucratization, he said.

The leader called on all levels, sectors, organizations, businesses, and individuals domestically and internationally to continue accompanying, contributing resources, experience, and initiatives to build a united, compassionate, and safe society where no one is left behind.

Looking towards the 100th anniversary of the Society's founding, he emphasized the goal of building a society where compassion becomes a way of life, each community has the capacity for self-protection and mutual support; everyone in distress receives timely help and has the opportunity to recover and rise.

Earlier, in her commemorative speech, President of the Vietnam Red Cross Society Do Thi Thu Thao stated that during the 2022 - 2026 term, the total value of humanitarian activities of the Society exceeded VND21.1 trillion (nearly $820 million), assisting over 52 million people in difficult and vulnerable situations.

For the 2026 - 2031 period, the Society aims to continue innovating its operational methods, focusing on people as the center, communities as the foundation, digital transformation, and innovation as the driving force; shifting from post-disaster relief to early warning, early action, livelihood support, and capacity recovery for people.
The Society also focuses on digitizing activities, enhancing transparency in mobilizing, receiving, and distributing resources, and expanding cooperation domestically and internationally.

At the ceremony, General Secretary and President To Lam awarded the First-Class Labor Order for the second time to the Vietnam Red Cross Society, recognizing the Society's contributions to social welfare, charity, humanitarian work, and the nation's development.

At the ceremony, General Secretary and President Lam and other Party and State leaders launched the National Digital Humanitarian Portal, a platform designed to connect users, provide information and update the public on humanitarian activities nationwide.
